title: Waste collection contract and Trees for Woolwich funding deferral
subtitle: Roundabout designs, traffic controls, Habitat for Humanity water agreement, development tracking system and transit service changes also featured.
overview: The Planning and Works Committee recommended an eight-year, roughly $285 million contract with Emterra Environmental for cart-based garbage and green bin collection starting in March 2026. Staff said the higher cost reflects truck prices and labour, and that bringing collection in-house would not be cheaper. Residents will receive new carts, with a communications plan due later this year.

The committee heard a delegation from Trees for Woolwich asking the Region to match $50,000 a year for two years for roadside tree planting. It waived notice to allow a funding motion, then deferred that motion to August 2024 pending a staff report, because no funding source is identified and the request falls outside the budget process.

The committee also recommended a roundabout design at Strasburg Road and New Dundee Road, expropriation steps for a roundabout at Fischer Hallman Road and New Dundee Road, new traffic controls in several cities and Woolwich, a water infrastructure agreement with Habitat for Humanity, and the sale of surplus land in Cambridge. Council will consider these recommendations later. Staff also presented growth data and a development tracking system, received for information.

decisions.detail: The committee recommended accepting Emterra Environmental's proposal for automated cart-based and manual waste collection and cart supply for eight years from March 2026, with two optional one-year renewals {{vote:m11}}.
The committee deferred the motion to support $50,000 a year for two years to August 2024, pending a staff report on funding {{vote:m3}}.

decisions.item: Strasburg Road and New Dundee Road roundabout
decisions.detail: The committee recommended approving the multi-lane roundabout design in Kitchener, with related speed limit, lane designation and pedestrian crossover by-law changes after construction.

decisions.item: Fischer Hallman and New Dundee expropriation
decisions.detail: The committee recommended authorizing the Regional Solicitor to begin expropriation of partial land takings and temporary easements in Kitchener and North Dumfries for a roundabout.

decisions.item: Habitat for Humanity water infrastructure agreement
decisions.detail: The committee recommended an agreement with Habitat for Humanity Waterloo Region for relocating critical water infrastructure at 100 St George St, Kitchener {{vote:m9}}, with a plan to add it to that evening's Special Council.
The committee recommended new pedestrian crossovers, a school bus loading zone, no-right-turn-on-red restrictions and lower speed limits on Bleams Road at various locations {{vote:m10}}.
The committee recommended declaring the Cambridge lands surplus and authorizing their sale to Skyline Commercial Real Estate Holdings Inc. for $50,000.

decisions.item: Grand River Source Protection Plan amendment
decisions.detail: The committee recommended supporting the updated source protection technical assessment for Waterloo Region in the draft amended plan.

debate: On Trees for Woolwich, the delegate said volunteer-based planting costs about $15 per tree, far below the Region's own cost, and that the requested funding would complete the project. Supporters called the ask reasonable.

Those favouring deferral said no funding source was identified and that adding unbudgeted requests outside the budget process sets a precedent as other municipalities seek similar support. A delegate and some councillors said a late-year decision would miss fall planting, since trees must be sourced well ahead.

On the development tracking system, several councillors questioned spending about $2 million when Bill 23 may shift planning duties to area municipalities, and cited long regional review times. Staff said the system would be adaptable, that the Region would keep a role, and that technology is only one part of improving processes. Others noted the funding was already budgeted.

On the waste contract, councillors asked why operating costs would roughly double. Staff pointed to a 50 per cent rise in truck costs over four years and to labour costs, said in-house collection would not be cheaper, and warned that not approving would risk service after March 2026. Councillors also asked about downtown service, in-person business area consultation and accessibility.
A student association delegate supported the Route 62 changes but asked for a stop closer to the Conestoga campus, shelter and lighting, and a review of the one-way loop and lack of weekend service.
